items.body: The two gubernatorial candidates met October 1 in Eugene for their first debate since 2022, clashing on homelessness, affordability, schools, and the economy, with Drazan arguing Kotek has failed on each. Kotek declined a July debate and no Portland debate will be held this cycle, breaking a decades long KGW tradition; the next debates are October 7 in Medford and October 13 in Bend.
items.headline: Kotek and Drazan spar in first debate of 2026 rematch

items.body: The Portland City Council voted to deprioritize police enforcement against psychedelics, framing the move as support for veterans, first responders, and Portlanders using them for mental health healing. The vote came as Oregon's psilocybin program got a reprieve: the Oregon Health Authority dropped its controversial plan to double licensing fees after industry pushback.
items.headline: Portland council votes to deprioritize psychedelics enforcement

items.body: Portland General Electric said it may abandon its holding company reorganization after the Oregon Public Utility Commission approved it with conditions PGE calls too strict, including dividend limits tied to retained earnings and credit ratings. The order includes about $83 million in customer benefits and rate credits that would only take effect if the reorganization proceeds; PGE shares fell about 6.5% on analyst downgrades in the same week.
items.headline: PGE stalls on holding company plan after regulators impose conditions

items.body: Portland announced Braiden Bell as its new TV play by play voice, then fired him roughly eight hours later when offensive tweets from 2012-2013 surfaced. The episode sparked a split reaction: supporters of the move cited accountability, while critics noted Bell was 15 at the time and blamed the team's vetting process.
items.headline: Trail Blazers fire broadcaster Braiden Bell hours after hiring

items.body: OHSU neurosurgeons became the first in Oregon to implant vagus nerve stimulation devices, one to treat rheumatoid arthritis and one to aid stroke rehabilitation.
items.headline: First vagus nerve implants in Oregon

items.body: OHSU enrolled the first West Coast participant in a CRISPR Therapeutics trial targeting the ANGPTL3 liver gene to treat severe high cholesterol.
items.headline: First West Coast CRISPR cholesterol trial participant

items.body: A fisherman trapped under a boulder on the Oregon coast used Siri to call 911 and was flown to OHSU Hospital with severe facial injuries.
items.headline: Fisherman rescued via Siri, recovering at OHSU

items.body: Upcoming lectures and seminars for the coming week will be listed here in each Monday edition.
items.headline: Campus events

items.body: Both campaigns' clips went viral and comment sections turned into partisan battles over homelessness and taxes.
items.headline: The Kotek/Drazan debate dominated local feeds

items.body: Fans split between excitement for the Ja and Dame pairing and a separate heated debate about the Bell firing and cancel culture.
items.headline: Dame Time's return lit up Blazers fans

items.body: A viral street interview series documenting the fentanyl and homelessness crisis drew millions of views and revived the Measure 110 repeal debate.
items.headline: Drug crisis interviews drew millions of views

items.body: A clip of federal agents making a nighttime arrest on September 27 drew heated responses about immigration enforcement in the city.
items.headline: Federal arrest clip sparked immigration debate
The governor's race is the city's dominant story, with the first Kotek/Drazan debate and more to come in Medford and Bend.
City policy moved progressive while statewide drug politics stayed heated: psychedelics enforcement deprioritized as the fentanyl crisis debate raged online.
PGE's restructuring trouble signals regulatory headwinds for the region's utility.
Sports and culture moments (Dame's return, the Bell firing) gave Portlanders lighter things to argue about.
OHSU had a strong research week with first-in-region vagus nerve implants and a landmark CRISPR trial.

editions.theme: The race for Oregon governor took over the week: Tina Kotek and Christine Drazan met in their first debate of the rematch, while the city council pushed progressive drug policy and Portland General Electric stumbled into a regulatory fight.

name: Portland
summary: Weekly briefing on Portland, Oregon: city news, OHSU, and local conversation.
